{
 "path": "d:\\文档\\Cursor\\EDM\\edm-backend\\app\\models\\sender_health.py",
 "contents": "\"\"\"Sender-identity health snapshots.\n\nPersisted row-per-check so operators (and ``create_send_task``) can read\n\"the most recent SPF/DKIM/DMARC/PTR/TLS verdict for this From address\"\nwithout hammering DNS / SMTP on every request.\n\nOne row per (from_email, purpose, checked_at). ``purpose`` tracks the\nmarketing / transactional split introduced in Phase 0 so that a clean\ntransactional domain's pass doesn't mask a broken marketing domain.\n\"\"\"\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\nfrom sqlalchemy import Boolean, DateTime, Index, String, Text\nfrom sqlalchemy.dialects.sqlite import JSON\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column\n\nfrom app.models.base import Base\n\n\nclass SenderHealth(Base):\n    __tablename__ = \"sender_health\"\n    __table_args__ = (\n        # Common lookup: latest record for (from_email, purpose)\n        Index(\n            \"ix_sender_health_from_purpose_checked\",\n            \"from_email\",\n            \"purpose\",\n            \"checked_at\",\n        ),\n    )\n\n    # Normalised sender address (lowercase). Kept as plain string because\n    # the FROM address can legitimately come from an env var that isn't\n    # in any ``users``/``campaigns`` FK.\n    from_email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=False)\n\n    # \"marketing\" | \"transactional\" | \"unknown\" — drives the\n    # create_send_task gate: marketing campaigns must use the marketing\n    # identity, transactional flows must use the transactional one.\n    purpose: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20), nullable=False, default=\"marketing\")\n\n    # Per-axis booleans. ``None`` means \"not checked yet\" — e.g. DKIM is\n    # only useful once we know which selector Tencent assigned; an offline\n    # environment can leave DKIM None without failing the row outright.\n    spf_ok: Mapped[bool | None] = mapped_column(Boolean)\n    dkim_ok: Mapped[bool | None] = mapped_column(Boolean)\n    dmarc_ok: Mapped[bool | None] = mapped_column(Boolean)\n    ptr_ok: Mapped[bool | None] = mapped_column(Boolean)\n    tls_ok: Mapped[bool | None] = mapped_column(Boolean)\n\n    # Summarised top-level verdict: pass = every checked axis ok; warn =\n    # at least one axis failed but isn't a hard blocker (e.g. PTR); fail\n    # = SPF/DKIM/DMARC broken. The gate in create_send_task refuses to\n    # run when overall_status == 'fail'.\n    overall_status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(\n        String(10), nullable=False, default=\"unknown\"\n    )\n\n    # Structured per-axis findings — raw DNS records, selectors tried,\n    # observed TLS cipher, PTR hostname, etc. Useful for the dashboard\n    # \"why is this failing?\" drill-down without re-running DNS.\n    detail: Mapped[dict | None] = mapped_column(JSON)\n\n    # Free-form notes (mostly the first human-readable reason we rejected).\n    # Separate from ``detail`` so the dashboard can show a one-liner\n    # without traversing JSON.\n    summary: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text)\n\n    # When the check ran. ``created_at`` tracks the insert time, this\n    # tracks the logical \"as-of\" moment. They'll usually match but we\n    # keep them separate so seeded / back-filled rows read correctly.\n    checked_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(\n        DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False\n    )\n"
}

Looking at the PTR check, there's a subtle bug — when all IPs fail the PTR lookup, we return `ok=None` instead of `False`. Let me fix:

 The real domain validation is working as expected—SPF, DKIM, and TLS all check out, DMARC exists but with a permissive policy that I'm flagging as a warning, and the missing PTR record is a soft warning since that's typical for Tencent's infrastructure. I'm noticing a bug in the PTR check logic though—when we attempt to resolve PTRs but they all fail, the function returns `ok=None` instead of `False`. The issue is that `seen_any` stays False after failed attempts, and `r.ok = seen_any or None` evaluates to None instead of False. I need to fix that so it properly distinguishes between "never attempted" and "attempted but failed."

### 🤖 Agent

Let me create a dedicated module for unsubscribe-coverage checks:

 The envelope template always includes an Unsubscribe link, but it only works properly when both `campaign_id` and `recipient_id` are provided — otherwise it defaults to `#`, which doesn't actually unsubscribe the user when clicked.

Legacy email bodies that start with `<table>` bypass the envelope entirely, so they need their own unsubscribe link built in. The plain template flow uses `promotion_v1.html` which also has the same `{{ unsubscribe_url|default('#') }}` pattern.

I need to build a send-time validation check that scans the final rendered HTML for visible unsubscribe markers (in multiple languages like "Unsubscribe", "退订", "配信停止", etc.) and confirms there's an actual `<a>` tag with a real URL attached, not just a `#`. I'll create this as a utility function in `unsubscribe_coverage.py` that returns a structured result, then call it from `SendService._send_one_email` as a last-chance gate before dispatch — if validation fails and strict mode is enabled, mark the send as failed with a clear reason; otherwise just log a warning.

For the content validator specifically, I should only enforce the check on legacy bodies since v2 envelopes handle the footer automatically. The real substance of the plan is ensuring that Writer-generated legacy content always includes a visible, functional unsubscribe link.

- 🔧 **Write**

{
 "path": "d:\\文档\\Cursor\\EDM\\edm-backend\\app\\services\\unsubscribe_coverage.py",
 "contents": "\"\"\"Visible-unsubscribe-link coverage utility.\n\nPhase 0 of the 50w EDM按时送达 plan. Yahoo / Gmail / Apple Mail bulk\nguidelines all require **two** layers of unsubscribe:\n\n1. The ``List-Unsubscribe`` RFC 2369 / 8058 SMTP header (handled in\n   :mod:`app.services.tencent_smtp_client` — done).\n2. A **visible** unsubscribe link or instruction inside the rendered\n   email body. Header-only opt-out shows up on Outlook as \"Manage\n   subscription\" but breaks entirely on webmail / niche clients, which\n   is precisely where Yahoo's 2-day SLA starts ticking.\n\nThis module is the body-side coverage check. It scans a rendered HTML\npayload for a visible unsubscribe affordance in the major shipping\nlocales (zh-CN / zh-TW / en / ja / ko / de / fr / es / pt) and returns\na structured verdict callers can either:\n\n* hard-fail on (content-validator, at write time — for legacy bodies that\n  manage their own footer),\n* or fall back to warn+log (send-time, as a belt-and-suspenders check\n  right before dispatch).\n\nWe also explicitly reject the ``href=\"#\"`` placeholder that the envelope\ntemplate emits when ``unsubscribe_url`` wasn't passed in — a dead link\nis worse than no link because the recipient clicks, sees no effect, and\nreports as spam instead.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\n# ── Patterns ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n# Visible anchor text that signals \"this is how to opt out\". We accept\n# a generous multilingual set — English variants, Simplified/Traditional\n# Chinese, Japanese (配信停止 / 配信解除), Korean (구독 취소 / 수신 거부),\n# German (abmelden), French (se désabonner), Spanish (cancelar\n# suscripción), Portuguese (cancelar inscrição).\n_VISIBLE_TEXT_RE = re.compile(\n    r\"unsubscribe\"\n    r\"|opt[\\s\\-]*out\"\n    r\"|stop[\\s\\-]*emails?\"\n    r\"|退订\"\n    r\"|取消订阅\"\n    r\"|取消訂閱\"\n    r\"|退订邮件\"\n    r\"|不再接收\"\n    r\"|不再接收此类邮件\"\n    r\"|配信停止\"\n    r\"|配信解除\"\n    r\"|メール配信を停止\"\n    r\"|구독\\s*취소\"\n    r\"|수신\\s*거부\"\n    r\"|abmelden\"\n    r\"|se\\s+desabonner\"\n    r\"|se\\s+désabonner\"\n    r\"|cancelar\\s+suscripci(?:ón|on)\"\n    r\"|cancelar\\s+inscri(?:ção|cao)\",\n    re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n# URL-path hint — any anchor whose href contains \"/unsubscribe\",\n# \"unsub\", \"optout\" or \"stop-emails\" counts as coverage even if the\n# visible text is purely iconographic. The encoder in\n# ``app.core.tracking_codec`` produces paths like\n# ``/t/u/<token>`` — we include that prefix too.\n_UNSUB_HREF_HINT_RE = re.compile(\n    r\"/unsubscribe\"\n    r\"|unsub\"\n    r\"|/opt[\\-_]?out\"\n    r\"|stop[\\-_]?emails?\"\n    r\"|/t/u/\",\n    re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n# Any <a href=\"...\"> — we pull the href out to (a) validate it isn't\n# a dead placeholder and (b) cross-check against _UNSUB_HREF_HINT_RE.\n_ANCHOR_RE = re.compile(\n    r\"\"\"<a\\s+[^>]*href\\s*=\\s*(?P<q>['\"])(?P<url>[^'\"]*)(?P=q)[^>]*>(?P<text>.*?)</a>\"\"\",\n    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL,\n)\n\n# Placeholder URLs that shouldn't count as real coverage.\n_DEAD_HREFS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(\n    {\"\", \"#\", \"javascript:void(0)\", \"about:blank\", \"mailto:\"}\n)\n\n\n# ── Data contract ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass UnsubscribeCoverage:\n    \"\"\"Outcome of a coverage scan.\n\n    Attributes\n    ----------\n    ok : bool\n        True when the HTML exposes at least one *usable* unsubscribe\n        link to the reader.\n    anchor_count : int\n        Number of ``<a>`` tags that looked like unsubscribe candidates\n        (by visible text or href hint). Useful for dashboards.\n    anchor_urls : list[str]\n        Hrefs of the qualifying anchors (lower-cased, as-is).\n    visible_text_found : bool\n        True if any locale's unsubscribe phrase appeared in the\n        visible body — anchor or not.\n    reason : str\n        Short one-liner summarising why ``ok`` is the value it is.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    ok: bool\n    anchor_count: int = 0\n    anchor_urls: list[str] | None = None\n    visible_text_found: bool = False\n    reason: str = \"\"\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.anchor_urls is None:\n            self.anchor_urls = []\n\n\n# ── Public API ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n\ndef scan_html(html: str) -> UnsubscribeCoverage:\n    \"\"\"Return a coverage verdict for a rendered email body.\n\n    The scan is tolerant — malformed HTML and template remnants still\n    parse because we rely on targeted regexes rather than a full DOM\n    walk. False-negatives cost us a hard-reject; false-positives leak a\n    deceptive email. We bias toward recall: if *any* anchor looks like\n    a real unsubscribe target, we pass.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not html or not html.strip():\n        return UnsubscribeCoverage(\n            ok=False,\n            reason=\"html is empty\",\n        )\n\n    visible_text_found = bool(_VISIBLE_TEXT_RE.search(html))\n\n    qualifying_urls: list[str] = []\n    for match in _ANCHOR_RE.finditer(html):\n        href_raw = (match.group(\"url\") or \"\").strip()\n        href = href_raw.lower()\n        inner_text = match.group(\"text\") or \"\"\n        # Strip any nested tags from the anchor text for the visible check.\n        plain_inner = re.sub(r\"<[^>]+>\", \"\", inner_text).strip()\n\n        has_visible_text = bool(_VISIBLE_TEXT_RE.search(plain_inner))\n        has_href_hint = bool(_UNSUB_HREF_HINT_RE.search(href)) if href else False\n\n        if not (has_visible_text or has_href_hint):\n            continue\n        if href in _DEAD_HREFS:\n            # Dead placeholder — explicitly skip. Worse than no link.\n            continue\n        if href.startswith(\"mailto:\") and len(href) <= len(\"mailto:\"):\n            continue\n        qualifying_urls.append(href_raw)\n\n    if qualifying_urls:\n        return UnsubscribeCoverage(\n            ok=True,\n            anchor_count=len(qualifying_urls),\n            anchor_urls=qualifying_urls,\n            visible_text_found=visible_text_found,\n            reason=f\"{len(qualifying_urls)} usable unsubscribe anchor(s)\",\n        )\n\n    if visible_text_found:\n        # Visible text but no usable anchor is a red flag — the reader\n        # sees \"Unsubscribe\" but can't click anywhere. We reject so the\n        # Writer / template can fix it.\n        return UnsubscribeCoverage(\n            ok=False,\n            anchor_count=0,\n            anchor_urls=[],\n            visible_text_found=True,\n            reason=(\n                \"unsubscribe text is present but no <a href> goes anywhere \"\n                \"(dead placeholder '#' / empty / missing)\"\n            ),\n        )\n\n    return UnsubscribeCoverage(\n        ok=False,\n        anchor_count=0,\n        anchor_urls=[],\n        visible_text_found=False,\n        reason=\"no visible unsubscribe link (neither text nor anchor hint)\",\n    )\n\n\ndef describe_gap(coverage: UnsubscribeCoverage) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return an operator-facing one-liner explaining the gap.\"\"\"\n    if coverage.ok:\n        return \"\"\n    if coverage.visible_text_found:\n        return (\n            \"unsubscribe 文案已出现但对应链接是 # 或空值：请确保 \"\n            \"<a href=\\\"{unsubscribe_url}\\\"> 不是占位符。\"\n        )\n    return (\n        \"html 中既没有可见的 Unsubscribe / 退订 文案，也没有指向 \"\n        \"/unsubscribe 的链接。请在页脚放置一条：\"\n        \"\\\"<a href=\\\\\\\"{unsubscribe_url}\\\\\\\">Unsubscribe</a>\\\" \"\n        \"对齐 Yahoo / Gmail bulk-sender 的 2-day 生效要求。\"\n    )\n"
}

Looking at the full picture now, the translator produces one CampaignContent record per language with only the canonical fields translated, while the base language retains the full variant pool. When dispatching to recipients in non-base languages, the system falls back to the canonical subject and preheader since those languages don't have their own variants. The variant requirement only applies to the writer through `validate_content` with `require_variants=True`, so the translator's use of `validate_translation` sidesteps that check entirely. This means the current implementation is actually correct—translators don't need to produce variants, and the variant pool stays language-agnostic for dispatch purposes. So the dispatcher will use canonical fields as a fallback when variants aren't available, and pull the selected variant's fields when they exist. I'm also making sure the frontend can round-trip subject_variants through the content editing flow, and checking that validation doesn't break for translations or legacy code paths that don't expect variants.

 "new_string": "    def _render_for_job(self, job: _SendJob, ctx: _SendContext) -> tuple[str, str, str | None]:\n        \"\"\"Render (subject, html_body, unsub_url) for one job — pure, no I/O.\n\n        Phase 1 (50w EDM ramp) applies the variant-specific overrides\n        **before** wrapping the html_body in the envelope so the\n        subject visible in the inbox (envelope `<title>` + H1) matches\n        the variant the recipient was bucketed into.\n        \"\"\"\n        content_obj = ctx.contents.get((job.segment or \"\", job.lang or \"\"))\n        content_dict = _content_to_dict(content_obj) if content_obj else {}\n\n        # ── Variant resolution (subject / preheader / greeting / opening /\n        # cta_text / utm_term) ─────────────────────────────────────────\n        variant = _resolve_variant(content_obj, job.variant_idx)\n        canonical_subject = (\n            content_dict.get(\"subject\")\n            or (content_obj.email_title if content_obj else None)\n            or \"TapNow\"\n        )\n        canonical_preheader = content_dict.get(\"preheader\", \"\") or \"\"\n        canonical_cta_text = content_dict.get(\"cta_text\", \"\") or \"\"\n        canonical_cta_url = content_dict.get(\"cta_url\", \"\") or \"\"\n\n        if variant is not None:\n            subject = variant.get(\"subject\") or canonical_subject\n            preheader = variant.get(\"preheader\") or canonical_preheader\n            opening_paragraph = variant.get(\"opening_paragraph\") or \"\"\n            variant_cta_text = variant.get(\"cta_text\") or canonical_cta_text\n            utm_term = (variant.get(\"utm_term\") or \"\").strip()\n            # ``greeting`` is applied by rewriting any ``{greeting}`` or\n            # first-child ``<h2>``-level greeting is Writer's contract;\n            # we expose it through content_dict in case a legacy\n            # Jinja2 path (else branch below) needs it.\n            variant_greeting = variant.get(\"greeting\") or \"\"\n            if variant_greeting:\n                content_dict[\"greeting\"] = variant_greeting\n        else:\n            subject = canonical_subject\n            preheader = canonical_preheader\n            opening_paragraph = \"\"\n            variant_cta_text = canonical_cta_text\n            utm_term = \"\"\n\n        if content_obj and _has_html_body(content_dict):\n            html_fragment = content_dict[\"html_body\"]\n            html_fragment = _apply_variant_to_html(\n                html_body=html_fragment,\n                opening_paragraph=opening_paragraph,\n                cta_text=variant_cta_text,\n                cta_url=canonical_cta_url,\n                utm_term=utm_term,\n            )\n            html_body = template_engine.render_envelope(\n                html_body=html_fragment,\n                subject=subject,\n                preheader=preheader,\n                lang=content_dict.get(\"lang\", job.lang or \"en\"),\n                campaign_id=ctx.campaign_id,\n                recipient_id=job.recipient_id or \"\",\n                background_image_url=ctx.background_image_url,\n            )\n        elif content_obj and ctx.tpl_html:\n            seg_cfg = ctx.segment_configs.get(job.segment or \"\")\n            tracking_params = seg_cfg.tracking_params if seg_cfg else None\n            #  I'm refactoring the send task handler to use a worker pool pattern with an async queue and rate limiting—producers will feed jobs into the queue while multiple workers process them concurrently, each managing its own session and applying rate limits before sending through SMTP.

The tricky part is that the ratelimiter needs a `variant_idx` hint, but that field doesn't exist on SendLog yet since it's part of Phase 1 work. For the actual worker pool implementation, I'm thinking through the database session strategy—hammering SQLite with a new session per message across 30 workers could create contention on the WAL. I'll have each worker maintain its own session for the lifetime of the worker, batching updates to SendLog and Recipient rows in transactions, with a separate monitor task handling periodic aggregate counter flushes. The core flow is: producer queues SendJob objects, workers pull jobs and apply rate limiting before calling `send_many` with a batch, then commit the results in one transaction.

Now I'm working through the rate limiter interaction with batching—tokens should be acquired per email, not per batch, so the worker dequeues up to SEND_BATCH_SIZE items, acquires tokens for each one serially, then sends the batch together. The token acquisition itself acts as the rate limiter; batching is purely for connection reuse efficiency.

── Introspection ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    @property\n    def target_rate(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"The \"100% of intended throughput\" knob (owned by feedback loop).\"\"\"\n        return self._target_rate\n\n    @property\n    def ramp_ratio(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Ratio currently applied by the warmup ramp (0.0..1.0).\"\"\"\n        return self._ramp_ratio\n\n    @property\n    def max_rate(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Hard ceiling — feedback loop's scale_target never exceeds this.\"\"\"\n        return self._max_rate\n\n    @property\n    def current_rate(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Effective rate used to space batches = target × ramp, clamped.\"\"\"\n        effective = self._target_rate * self._ramp_ratio\n        return max(_MIN_RATE, min(effective, self._max_rate))\n\n    def snapshot(self) -> dict:\n        \"\"\"Return a JSON-safe snapshot for logging / feedback telemetry.\"\"\"\n        return {\n            \"target_rate\": round(self._target_rate, 3),\n            \"ramp_ratio\": round(self._ramp_ratio, 3),\n            \"current_rate\": round(self.current_rate, 3),\n            \"max_rate\": round(self._max_rate, 3),\n        }\n\n    # ── Knob setters ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    def set_target_rate(self, rate: float) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Overwrite the target — used when the operator changes a setting.\"\"\"\n        self._target_rate = max(_MIN_RATE, min(float(rate), self._max_rate))\n        return self._target_rate\n\n    def set_ramp_ratio(self, ratio: float) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Update the warmup ramp ratio (0..1). Called by RampController.\"\"\"\n        self._ramp_ratio = max(0.0, min(float(ratio), 1.0))\n        return self._ramp_ratio\n\n    def scale_target(self, factor: float) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Multiply ``target_rate`` by ``factor``, clamped to ``[_MIN_RATE, max_rate]``.\n\n        Returns the new target. Used by the feedback loop to down-scale on\n        bounce/defer spikes and to up-scale when progress lags but health\n        is clean.\n        \"\"\"\n        self._target_rate = max(\n            _MIN_RATE,\n            min(self._target_rate * max(0.0, float(factor)), self._max_rate),\n        )\n        return self._target_rate\n\n    # ── Scheduling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    async def acquire(self, n: int = 1) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Block until ``n`` emissions are allowed under the current rate.\n\n        Returns the number of seconds slept (useful in tests / traces).\n        \"\"\"\n        if n <= 0:\n            return 0.0\n\n        async with self._lock:\n            now = time.monotonic()\n            rate = self.current_rate\n            slot_width = n / rate\n            # Don't let idle drift mint burst credit — clamp forward.\n            if self._next_slot < now:\n                self._next_slot = now\n            deadline = self._next_slot\n            self._next_slot += slot_width\n            wait = deadline - now\n\n        if wait > 0:\n            await asyncio.sleep(wait)\n            return wait\n        return 0.0\n"
}

The tricky part is coordinating when both the ramp and feedback loop want to modify the rate — they'd be writing to the same global bucket, and whichever writes last wins. The cleanest approach is to give the limiter two separate inputs: a target rate and a ramp ratio, then always compute the effective rate as `target × ratio`. That way the feedback loop sets the target, the ramp controller sets the ratio, and the limiter handles the multiplication internally.  "contents": "\"\"\"Rate-knob coordinator between the Phase 3 ramp / feedback loops and\nthe Phase 2 :class:`app.services.send_ratelimiter.SendRateLimiter`.\n\nWhy this module exists\n----------------------\nThe warm-up ramp and the feedback loop both want to steer the *global*\nsend rate, but for different reasons:\n\n* **RampController** slowly multiplies the target by ``0.10 → 0.25 →\n  0.50 → 1.0`` over the first 10 minutes (Gmail's \"don't burst from\n  cold start\" rule).\n* **FeedbackLoop** scales the target up or down by 10-30 % based on\n  SMTP 4xx / bounce / spam signals, within a hard ceiling\n  (``SEND_GLOBAL_RATE_PER_SEC_MAX``).\n\nIf both call ``limiter.set_global_rate`` directly they fight each other\n(last writer wins). ``SendPacer`` owns the two independent dimensions —\n``target_rate`` (feedback's knob) and ``ramp_ratio`` (ramp's knob) — and\npushes the *multiplied* effective rate into the underlying limiter\nevery time either knob moves. The feedback loop gets a stable ``target``\nto scale even while the ramp is still below 100 %.\n\nKeeping this module 100 % pure Python (no DB / no network) means it\nunit-tests without an event loop: a test can pass its own ``sink``\ncallable and assert the sequence of effective rates emitted.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Callable\n\nfrom app.core.logging_config import get_logger\n\nlogger = get_logger(\"send_pacer\")\n\n# Hard floor — the ratelimiter bucket cannot have rate <= 0 and we don't\n# want to grind to a halt silently just because the feedback loop went\n# trigger-happy with down-scaling. Anything this low is a \"we're about\n# to pause\" signal anyway; the feedback loop will set status=paused\n# before we approach it.\n_MIN_RATE = 0.1\n\n\nclass SendPacer:\n    \"\"\"Single source of truth for ``current_global_rate`` decisions.\n\n    Two knobs, one output::\n\n        effective = clamp(target_rate × ramp_ratio, [_MIN_RATE, max_rate])\n\n    Both knobs expose their own setter so callers can mutate *only* the\n    dimension they own. Each mutator calls the optional ``sink`` callable\n    with the new effective rate; in production this is\n    ``SendRateLimiter.set_global_rate``. Tests pass a local capture to\n    assert ordering without needing the full limiter.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        *,\n        initial_target_rate: float,\n        max_rate: float,\n        initial_ramp_ratio: float = 1.0,\n        sink: Callable[[float], None] | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        target = max(_MIN_RATE, float(initial_target_rate))\n        cap = max(target, float(max_rate))\n        self._target_rate = target\n        self._max_rate = cap\n        self._ramp_ratio = max(0.0, min(float(initial_ramp_ratio), 1.0))\n        self._sink = sink\n        # Emit an initial value so the underlying limiter starts at the\n        # correct rate even before anyone moves a knob. Idempotent — the\n        # limiter's set_global_rate is safe to call repeatedly.\n        self._emit()\n\n    # ── Introspection ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    @property\n    def target_rate(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Knob owned by the feedback loop (feedback scales this).\"\"\"\n        return self._target_rate\n\n    @property\n    def ramp_ratio(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Knob owned by the ramp controller (0.0..1.0).\"\"\"\n        return self._ramp_ratio\n\n    @property\n    def max_rate(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Hard ceiling — target is clamped here, effective can't exceed.\"\"\"\n        return self._max_rate\n\n    @property\n    def current_rate(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Effective rate = ``target × ramp_ratio``, clamped to ``[_MIN_RATE, max_rate]``.\"\"\"\n        effective = self._target_rate * self._ramp_ratio\n        return max(_MIN_RATE, min(effective, self._max_rate))\n\n    def snapshot(self) -> dict:\n        \"\"\"Return a JSON-safe snapshot for logging / feedback telemetry.\"\"\"\n        return {\n            \"target_rate\": round(self._target_rate, 3),\n            \"ramp_ratio\": round(self._ramp_ratio, 3),\n            \"current_rate\": round(self.current_rate, 3),\n            \"max_rate\": round(self._max_rate, 3),\n        }\n\n    # ── Mutators ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    def set_target_rate(self, rate: float) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Overwrite the target — typically from operator / feedback loop.\"\"\"\n        self._target_rate = max(_MIN_RATE, min(float(rate), self._max_rate))\n        self._emit()\n        return self._target_rate\n\n    def set_ramp_ratio(self, ratio: float) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Update the warm-up ratio (0..1). Called by :class:`RampController`.\"\"\"\n        self._ramp_ratio = max(0.0, min(float(ratio), 1.0))\n        self._emit()\n        return self._ramp_ratio\n\n    def scale_target(self, factor: float) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Multiply ``target`` by ``factor``, clamped to ``[_MIN_RATE, max_rate]``.\n\n        Returns the new target. Used by the feedback loop to down-scale\n        on bounce/defer/spam spikes and to up-scale when progress lags\n        but health is clean.\n        \"\"\"\n        previous = self._target_rate\n        self._target_rate = max(\n            _MIN_RATE,\n            min(self._target_rate * max(0.0, float(factor)), self._max_rate),\n        )\n        if self._target_rate != previous:\n            self._emit()\n        return self._target_rate\n\n    # ── Sink management ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    def attach_sink(self, sink: Callable[[float], None]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Late-bind the sink (e.g., limiter wired after construction) and emit once.\"\"\"\n        self._sink = sink\n        self._emit()\n\n    def _emit(self) -> None:\n        if self._sink is None:\n            return\n        try:\n            self._sink(self.current_rate)\n        except Exception:\n            logger.exception(\n                \"SendPacer sink raised | effective_rate=%.3f snapshot=%s\",\n                self.current_rate, self.snapshot(),\n            )\n"

Actually, let me restructure this so tokens are acquired lazily right before sending, not when the job enters the batch. That way if pause_flag triggers, we haven't wasted any tokens yet — we just clear the pending batch and those jobs stay marked as pending in the database for the next resume cycle.

 "new_string": "    async def send_email(\n        self,\n        to_email: str,\n        subject: str,\n        html_content: str,\n        from_email: str | None = None,\n        unsubscribe_url: str | None = None,\n        unsubscribe_mailto: str | None = None,\n    ) -> SESResult:\n        sender = from_email or self._user\n        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()\n        return await loop.run_in_executor(\n            None,\n            partial(\n                self._send_sync,\n                to_email, subject, html_content, sender,\n                unsubscribe_url, unsubscribe_mailto,\n            ),\n        )\n\n    async def send_many(\n        self,\n        messages: list[dict],\n        from_email: str | None = None,\n    ) -> list[SESResult]:\n        \"\"\"Sequential shim so the Phase 3 batch path works on Gmail too.\n\n        Gmail's SMTP daily cap means nobody should be sending bulk\n        production mail through this client, so there's no point in\n        implementing a real keep-alive session pool — we loop over\n        :meth:`send_email` one at a time. The Phase 3 batch retry still\n        works on top because each result is a proper :class:`SESResult`.\n        \"\"\"\n        results: list[SESResult] = []\n        for msg in messages:\n            res = await self.send_email(\n                to_email=msg[\"to_email\"],\n                subject=msg[\"subject\"],\n                html_content=msg[\"html_content\"],\n                from_email=from_email,\n                unsubscribe_url=msg.get(\"unsubscribe_url\"),\n                unsubscribe_mailto=msg.get(\"unsubscribe_mailto\"),\n            )\n            results.append(res)\n        return results"
}

Case 1: clean health, not lagging → no change\n    pacer, emits = make_pacer()\n    pause_flag = asyncio.Event()\n    loop = FeedbackLoop(pacer, task_id='t1', campaign_id='c1', defer_counter=DeferCounter(), pause_flag=pause_flag)\n    loop._apply_decision(make_metrics())\n    print('case 1 (steady):', pacer.snapshot(), 'pause=', pause_flag.is_set())\n    assert pacer.target_rate == 35.0\n\n    # Case 3: bounce > 2% → scale down 0.7\n    pacer, _ = make_pacer()\n    loop = FeedbackLoop(pacer, task_id='t1', campaign_id='c1', defer_counter=DeferCounter())\n    loop._apply_decision(make_metrics(delivered=700, bounced=50))  # bounce=50/750 ≈ 6.7%\n    print('case 3 (bounce spike):', pacer.snapshot())\n    assert abs(pacer.target_rate - 35 * 0.7) < 1e-6\n\n    # Case 4: defer > 5% → scale down 0.7\n    pacer, _ = make_pacer()\n    loop = FeedbackLoop(pacer, task_id='t1', campaign_id='c1', defer_counter=DeferCounter())\n    defer = {'attempts': 100, 'defers': 10, 'permanent': 0, 'successes': 90, 'defer_rate': 0.10, 'recent_errors': ['SMTP 421']}\n    loop._apply_decision(make_metrics(defer=defer))\n    print('case 4 (defer spike):', pacer.snapshot())\n    assert abs(pacer.target_rate - 35 * 0.7) < 1e-6\n\n    # Case 5: spam ≥ 0.3% → hard stop\n    pacer, _ = make_pacer()\n    pause_flag = asyncio.Event()\n    loop = FeedbackLoop(pacer, task_id='t1', campaign_id='c1', defer_counter=DeferCounter(), pause_flag=pause_flag)\n    loop._apply_decision(make_metrics(delivered=1000, spam_reports=5))  # spam_rate = 0.005 = 0.5%\n    print('case 5 (hard stop):', pacer.snapshot(), 'pause_req=', loop.pause_requested, 'flag=', pause_flag.is_set())\n    assert loop.pause_requested is True\n    assert pause_flag.is_set() is True\n\n    # ## Phase 3 交付清单

### p3-sendmany — SMTP `send_many` 批发集成
- **`_process_batch`** ([send_service.py](edm-backend/app/services/send_service.py)): 渲染 → 按域/变体获取令牌 → `send_many` 批发 → 反馈计数 → 持久化，一次 DB session 一个批次
- **`_dispatch_batch_with_retry`** / **`_dispatch_batch`**: batch 级别的指数退避重试（对 4xx 非永久失败），不污染 reputation；`getattr(self._ses, "send_many", ...)` 让没实现批发的后端（老 Mock / Gmail）自动退化为串行 `send_email`
- **Worker 聚批**: `_send_worker` 把单 `await queue.get()` 改成 pending_batch 累积，达到 `SES_SMTP_BATCH_SIZE`（默认 20）或拿到 sentinel 时才 flush；暂停时保留 pending 行待恢复
- 补齐了 [mock_ses.py](edm-backend/app/mocks/mock_ses.py) 和 [gmail_client.py](edm-backend/app/services/gmail_client.py) 的 `send_many` 垫片，保持接口一致

### p3-warmup — 10/25/50/100% ramp + 指纹强制重 ramp
- **`SendPacer`** ([send_pacer.py](edm-backend/app/services/send_pacer.py)): target × ramp_ratio 两维度独立旋钮 + sink callback 推到 `SendRateLimiter.set_global_rate`，ramp 和 feedback 不再争抢
- **`RampController`** ([send_ramp.py](edm-backend/app/services/send_ramp.py)): asyncio tick 每 30s 更新 `ramp_ratio`；`DEFAULT_SCHEDULE` 10→25→50→100% 覆盖 10 分钟，`FAMILIAR_SCHEDULE` 50→100% 覆盖 1 分钟
- **`SenderBaseline`** ([sender_baseline.py](edm-backend/app/models/sender_baseline.py) + 迁移 [9a1b2c3d4e5f](edm-backend/migrations/versions/9a1b2c3d4e5f_sender_baseline.py)): 按 `(from_email, smtp_host)` 记录 template_hash + last_full_speed_at
- **`SenderBaselineStore.should_force_fresh_ramp`**: 无 baseline / From 变 / SMTP host 变 / 模板 hash 变 / baseline 超 72h（`SEND_BASELINE_FULL_SPEED_GRACE_HOURS`）→ 强制全长 warmup
- ramp 跑完 100% 才 upsert baseline（paused 不算成功到顶）

### p3-feedback-loop — 30s 节奏闭环
- **`FeedbackLoop`** ([send_feedback_loop.py](edm-backend/app/services/send_feedback_loop.py)): 后台 asyncio 任务，每 `SEND_FEEDBACK_INTERVAL_SECONDS`（30s）执行一次决策
- **`DeferCounter`**: worker 在 `_process_batch` 后 `record_many(results)`，把 SMTP 4xx / non-permanent 失败喂给反馈环（区分 permanent 5xx）
- **信号源**: `TrackingEvent` 滚动 5 分钟窗口（delivered / bounce / spamreport）+ `SendTask.sent/total` 对比 `SEND_WINDOW_HOURS` 判 `progress_lagging`
- **决策表**:
  - `spam_rate ≥ 0.3%` → 立即 set `pause_flag` + 写 DB `status=paused`（`_persist_pause`）+ 再降一次速冷却 in-flight
  - `spam_rate ≥ 0.1%` → warn 日志，屏蔽当次 upscale
  - `bounce_rate > 2%` 或 `defer_rate > 5%` → `pacer.scale_target(0.7)`
  - 进度落后 + 健康 → `pacer.scale_target(1.1)`，自动在 `SEND_GLOBAL_RATE_PER_SEC_MAX=90` 处封顶

- [config.py](edm-backend/app/config.py): 新增 `SES_SMTP_BATCH_SIZE`、`SEND_RAMP_TICK_SECONDS`、`SEND_BASELINE_FULL_SPEED_GRACE_HOURS`、`SEND_RAMP_ENABLED`、`SEND_FEEDBACK_ENABLED`、`SEND_FEEDBACK_INTERVAL_SECONDS`、`SEND_FEEDBACK_WINDOW_SECONDS`、`SEND_DEFER_RATE_DOWNSCALE`（复用 Phase 2 的 `SEND_WINDOW_HOURS` / `SEND_GLOBAL_RATE_PER_SEC[_MAX]` / `SEND_BOUNCE_RATE_DOWNSCALE` / `SEND_SPAM_RATE_*`）

 "new_string": "    async def execute_send_task(self, task_id: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Execute a send task — designed to run as a background job.\n\n        Accepts ``queued`` / ``preparing`` as fresh-start states, and\n        ``paused`` as a resume path: a paused task keeps its\n        ``started_at`` and pending logs untouched, so re-entering is\n        just a matter of flipping status back to ``sending`` and\n        re-invoking :meth:`_process_send_task`, which picks up the\n        ``pending`` rows that were left behind when the worker pool\n        bailed out.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.info(\"Executing send task | task=%s\", task_id)\n\n        async with async_session_factory() as db:\n            task = await db.get(SendTask, task_id)\n            if not task:\n                logger.error(\"SendTask %s not found\", task_id)\n                return\n            if task.status not in (\"queued\", \"preparing\", \"paused\"):\n                logger.warning(\n                    \"SendTask %s in unexpected state '%s', skipping\",\n                    task_id, task.status,\n                )\n                return\n\n            resumed = task.status == \"paused\"\n            task.status = \"sending\"\n            if task.started_at is None:\n                task.started_at = _now()\n            if resumed:\n                # Reset any auto-pause annotation so the next pause line\n                # isn't confused with a prior incident.\n                task.error_message = None\n                task.completed_at = None\n            await db.commit()\n\n            campaign = await db.get(Campaign, task.campaign_id)\n            if campaign and campaign.status != \"sending\":\n                campaign.status = \"sending\"\n                await db.commit()\n\n            if resumed:\n                logger.info(\"SendTask %s resumed from paused\", task_id)\n\n        try:\n            await self._process_send_task(task_id)\n        except Exception:\n            logger.exception(\"Fatal error executing task %s\", task_id)\n            async with async_session_factory() as db:\n                task = await db.get(SendTask, task_id)\n                if task:\n                    task.status = \"failed\"\n                    task.error_message = \"Internal processing error\"\n                    task.completed_at = _now()\n                    campaign = await db.get(Campaign, task.campaign_id)\n                    if campaign:\n                        campaign.status = \"failed\"\n                    await db.commit()"
}

 "new_string": "    async def _send_worker(\n        self,\n        queue: asyncio.Queue,\n        limiter: SendRateLimiter,\n        counters: _SendCounters,\n        ctx: _SendContext,\n        pause_flag: asyncio.Event | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Single consumer coroutine.\n\n        Exits on any of:\n          - pulling the ``None`` sentinel (happy path);\n          - ``pause_flag`` being set by the pause-watcher (drains\n            remaining items without processing so other workers finish\n            too).\n        \"\"\"\n        while True:\n            job = await queue.get()\n            try:\n                if job is None:\n                    return\n                if pause_flag is not None and pause_flag.is_set():\n                    # Paused — don't dispatch this job. Leave the\n                    # SendLog row as ``pending`` for the resume path\n                    # to pick up.\n                    continue\n                try:\n                    await self._process_one_job(job, limiter, counters, ctx)\n                except Exception:\n                    # Never kill the whole pool over one bad recipient —\n                    # we log, mark the row failed, and keep going. A\n                    # dead worker would stall ~3% of the send (1/N).\n                    logger.exception(\n                        \"Worker unhandled error | task=%s log=%s to=%s\",\n                        ctx.campaign_id, job.log_id, job.recipient_email,\n                    )\n                    await self._mark_log_failed(job, error=\"worker_exception\")\n                    await counters.record(success=False, retries=settings.SEND_MAX_RETRIES)\n            finally:\n                queue.task_done()"

 "new_string": "    async def _pause_watcher(\n        self,\n        task_id: str,\n        stop: asyncio.Event,\n        pause_flag: asyncio.Event,\n        interval_seconds: float = 2.5,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Poll ``task.status`` and raise ``pause_flag`` when it flips to paused.\n\n        Exits promptly when ``stop`` fires (the progress flusher's\n        stop Event is reused — one signal, one cancellation point).\n        Any DB error is swallowed with a warning so a flaky DB doesn't\n        take the send pool down — the producer/finalize still make\n        progress, and the next tick will retry.\n        \"\"\"\n        while not stop.is_set():\n            try:\n                await asyncio.wait_for(stop.wait(), timeout=interval_seconds)\n                return\n            except asyncio.TimeoutError:\n                pass\n            try:\n                async with async_session_factory() as db:\n                    task = await db.get(SendTask, task_id)\n                    status = task.status if task else None\n            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n                logger.warning(\n                    \"Pause-watcher DB read failed | task=%s\", task_id,\n                    exc_info=True,\n                )\n                continue\n\n            if status in (\"paused\", \"cancelled\") and not pause_flag.is_set():\n                pause_flag.set()\n                logger.info(\n                    \"Pause-watcher: SendTask %s entered status=%s, raising pause flag\",\n                    task_id, status,\n                )\n                return\n\n    async def _persist_partial_progress(\n        self,\n        task_id: str,\n        *,\n        sent: int,\n        failed: int,\n        retries: int,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Flush counters to ``send_tasks`` without touching ``status``.\n\n        Used when the worker pool exits due to a pause — the status\n        column is already ``paused`` and we don't want to clobber it.\n        \"\"\"\n        try:\n            async with async_session_factory() as db:\n                await db.execute(\n                    update(SendTask)\n                    .where(SendTask.id == task_id)\n                    .values(sent=sent, failed=failed, retry_count=retries)\n                )\n                await db.commit()\n        except Exception:\n            logger.exception(\n                \"Partial-progress flush failed | task=%s sent=%d failed=%d\",\n                task_id, sent, failed,\n            )\n\n    async def _progress_flusher(\n        self,\n        task_id: str,\n        counters: _SendCounters,\n        stop: asyncio.Event,\n        interval_seconds: float = 2.0,\n    ) -> None:"
}

 "contents": "\"\"\"APScheduler integration for checking and executing scheduled send tasks.\n\nFour periodic jobs live here:\n\n- :func:`check_scheduled_tasks` — dispatches any queued task whose\n  ``scheduled_at`` has elapsed.\n- :func:`check_stale_tasks` — fails tasks that have been stuck in\n  ``sending`` beyond the dynamic stale threshold (``SEND_WINDOW_HOURS``\n  × 1.5, floored at 30 min so very short dev windows still give the\n  pipeline time to start).\n- :func:`recheck_sender_health` — Phase 0 DNS re-check so the dashboard\n  stays fresh even when no new campaigns trigger a send.\n- :func:`run_send_monitor` — Phase 4 red-line scan across every live\n  SendTask; auto-pauses tasks whose spam_rate crosses\n  ``SEND_SPAM_RATE_HARD_STOP``.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\n\nfrom apscheduler.schedulers.asyncio import AsyncIOScheduler\nfrom sqlalchemy import select\n\nfrom app.config import settings\nfrom app.core.logging_config import get_logger\nfrom app.database import async_session_factory\nfrom app.models.send_task import SendTask\n\nlogger = get_logger(\"scheduler\")\n\nscheduler = AsyncIOScheduler()\n\n# Stale threshold floor — even when SEND_WINDOW_HOURS is aggressive (e.g.\n# 0.1h for dev smoke tests) we still give the pipeline 30 min before\n# declaring a task dead. Matches the pre-Phase-4 behaviour.\n_STALE_THRESHOLD_FLOOR_SECONDS = 30 * 60\n\n\ndef _stale_threshold_seconds() -> float:\n    \"\"\"Dynamic stale threshold = ``SEND_WINDOW_HOURS * 1.5 * 3600`` seconds.\n\n    The plan in ``50w_edm_按时送达方案`` § Phase 4.2 says the stale\n    detector should be a function of the send window, not a hard 30-\n    minute constant — a 4 h window can legitimately sit in ``sending``\n    for 3-4 hours, and the old constant used to flip us to ``failed``\n    before the pool had even finished. 1.5× gives enough head-room for\n    the warm-up ramp + tail without losing the \"something is stuck\"\n    signal.\n    \"\"\"\n    window_seconds = max(float(settings.SEND_WINDOW_HOURS or 0.0), 0.0) * 3600.0\n    return max(window_seconds * 1.5, float(_STALE_THRESHOLD_FLOOR_SECONDS))\n\n\nasync def check_scheduled_tasks() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Find queued tasks whose scheduled_at <= now and execute them.\"\"\"\n    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)\n    logger.debug(\"Scheduler tick | checking for due tasks at %s\", now.isoformat())\n\n    async with async_session_factory() as db:\n        result = await db.execute(\n            select(SendTask)\n            .where(SendTask.status == \"queued\")\n            .where(SendTask.scheduled_at.isnot(None))\n            .where(SendTask.scheduled_at <= now)\n            .order_by(SendTask.scheduled_at)\n        )\n        due_tasks = result.scalars().all()\n        task_ids = [(t.id, t.campaign_id, t.scheduled_at) for t in due_tasks]\n\n    if not task_ids:\n        return\n\n    logger.info(\"Found %d due scheduled task(s)\", len(task_ids))\n\n    from app.services.send_service import send_service\n\n    for tid, cid, sched in task_ids:\n        logger.info(\n            \"Dispatching scheduled task | task=%s campaign=%s scheduled=%s\",\n            tid, cid, sched.isoformat() if sched else \"none\",\n        )\n        try:\n            await send_service.execute_send_task(tid)\n        except Exception:\n            logger.exception(\"Error executing scheduled task %s\", tid)\n\n\nasync def check_stale_tasks() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Mark tasks stuck in ``sending`` beyond the dynamic threshold as failed.\"\"\"\n    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)\n    threshold = _stale_threshold_seconds()\n\n    async with async_session_factory() as db:\n        result = await db.execute(\n            select(SendTask).where(SendTask.status == \"sending\")\n        )\n        sending_tasks = result.scalars().all()\n\n    for task in sending_tasks:\n        if task.started_at and (now - task.started_at).total_seconds() > threshold:\n            age_min = (now - task.started_at).total_seconds() / 60\n            logger.warning(\n                \"Marking stale task as failed | task=%s started=%s age_min=%.1f \"\n                \"threshold_min=%.1f\",\n                task.id, task.started_at.isoformat(), age_min, threshold / 60,\n            )\n            async with async_session_factory() as db:\n                stale = await db.get(SendTask, task.id)\n                if stale and stale.status == \"sending\":\n                    stale.status = \"failed\"\n                    stale.error_message = (\n                        f\"Task timed out (stale detection after \"\n                        f\"{threshold / 60:.0f}min)\"\n                    )\n                    stale.completed_at = now\n                    await db.commit()\n\n\nasync def recheck_sender_health() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 0 periodic recheck — refreshes the sender_health snapshot.\n\n    Runs off the main scheduler so operators see up-to-date SPF/DKIM/\n    DMARC verdicts on the dashboard even when nobody triggers a new\n    campaign for hours. No-op when the feature is disabled via\n    ``SENDER_HEALTH_CHECK_ENABLED``.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not settings.SENDER_HEALTH_CHECK_ENABLED:\n        return\n    try:\n        from app.services.sender_health import run_startup_check\n        await run_startup_check()\n    except Exception:\n        logger.exception(\"Sender health periodic recheck failed — will retry next cycle\")\n\n\nasync def run_send_monitor() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: scan live SendTasks against spam / bounce red-lines.\"\"\"\n    from app.services.send_monitor import monitor_active_tasks\n\n    try:\n        summary = await monitor_active_tasks()\n    except Exception:\n        logger.exception(\"send_monitor tick crashed\")\n        return\n\n    paused = summary.get(\"paused_now\") or []\n    warned = summary.get(\"warn\") or []\n    if paused or warned:\n        logger.info(\n            \"send_monitor tick | scanned=%d paused=%d warn=%d\",\n            summary.get(\"scanned\", 0), len(paused), len(warned),\n        )\n\n\ndef start_scheduler() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Register periodic jobs and start the scheduler.\"\"\"\n    if not settings.SCHEDULER_ENABLED:\n        logger.info(\"Scheduler disabled by config\")\n        return\n\n    scheduler.add_job(\n        check_scheduled_tasks,\n        \"interval\",\n        seconds=settings.SCHEDULER_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS,\n        id=\"check_scheduled_tasks\",\n        replace_existing=True,\n        max_instances=1,\n    )\n    scheduler.add_job(\n        check_stale_tasks,\n        \"interval\",\n        seconds=300,\n        id=\"check_stale_tasks\",\n        replace_existing=True,\n        max_instances=1,\n    )\n    recheck_seconds = settings.SENDER_HEALTH_RECHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS\n    if recheck_seconds and recheck_seconds > 0:\n        scheduler.add_job(\n            recheck_sender_health,\n            \"interval\",\n            seconds=recheck_seconds,\n            id=\"recheck_sender_health\",\n            replace_existing=True,\n            max_instances=1,\n        )\n\n    monitor_interval = max(int(settings.SEND_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SECONDS or 30), 5)\n    scheduler.add_job(\n        run_send_monitor,\n        \"interval\",\n        seconds=monitor_interval,\n        id=\"run_send_monitor\",\n        replace_existing=True,\n        max_instances=1,\n    )\n\n    scheduler.start()\n    logger.info(\n        \"Scheduler started | check_interval=%ds stale_threshold=%.0fmin \"\n        \"sender_health_recheck=%ds monitor=%ds\",\n        settings.SCHEDULER_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS,\n        _stale_threshold_seconds() / 60,\n        recheck_seconds if recheck_seconds > 0 else 0,\n        monitor_interval,\n    )\n\n\ndef stop_scheduler() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Gracefully shut down the scheduler.\"\"\"\n    if scheduler.running:\n        scheduler.shutdown(wait=False)\n        logger.info(\"Scheduler stopped\")\n"
}

### 🤖 Agent

Here's a summary of what was implemented for the three Phase 4 todos:

## [p4-preflight] 入口前置体检

**New file** `edm-backend/app/services/preflight.py` — runs all hard gates + soft warnings before `create_send_task` inserts any DB rows:

- **Sender identity health** — reads the most recent `sender_health` row for the active From; `fail` verdict → hard stop, `warn` / stale / missing → warning only. Gracefully degrades when the table is absent (brand-new deployment).
- **SES daily quota** — compares today's `send_logs` row count + planned recipients against `SEND_DAILY_QUOTA_LIMIT`. Zero = skip (the default).
- **Variant count** — counts both `subject_variants` JSON entries and distinct `(subject, preheader)` legacy pairs, enforces ≥ `SEND_MIN_VARIANTS`.
- **Recipient list** — checks the list exists, has rows, and matches `valid_count`.
- **Marketing ↔ transactional split** — refuses to send when `SES_FROM_EMAIL == SES_FROM_EMAIL_TRANSACTIONAL` (AGENTS.md 硬红线 #6).

`edm-backend/app/services/send_service.py::create_send_task` now runs this preflight after filtering recipients so the quota / variant checks see the actual planned send size.

`edm-backend/app/services/scheduler.py::check_stale_tasks` threshold is now `SEND_WINDOW_HOURS * 1.5 * 3600` (floored at 30 min).

## [p4-dashboard] 进度面板 + Postmaster 红线

**New file** `edm-backend/app/services/send_monitor.py` — single source of truth for:

- `compute_task_health(task_id)` → `sent_accepted`, `delivered`, `bounced`, `dropped`, `spam_rate`, `bounce_rate`, alert level (`ok` / `warn` / `hard_stop`).
- `compute_task_breakdown(task_id)` → per-`variant_idx` + per-recipient-domain counters (the two axes fingerprint-clustering penalties live in).
- `monitor_active_tasks()` — periodic coroutine registered with the scheduler, auto-pauses any task where `spam_rate ≥ SEND_SPAM_RATE_HARD_STOP` (0.3%) and logs warnings at 0.1%.
- `pause_task` / `resume_task` for the manual API path.

**New endpoints** in `edm-backend/app/api/send_tasks.py`:
- `GET /send-tasks/{id}/health`
- `GET /send-tasks/{id}/breakdown`
- `POST /send-tasks/{id}/pause`
- `POST /send-tasks/{id}/resume`
- `GET /send-tasks/monitor/dashboard` (aggregate + Yahoo SLA status)

`send_service.py` now wires a shared `asyncio.Event` into `_process_send_task`: a `_pause_watcher` coroutine polls `task.status` and flips the event when the monitor (or API) marks the task paused; workers drain their queue cleanly and the partial counters are persisted without clobbering the `paused` state. Resume re-runs `execute_send_task`, which accepts `paused` as a valid entry state and picks up the `pending` SendLogs.

## [p4-list-hygiene] 名单卫生

**New file** `edm-backend/app/services/suppression.py`:

- `build_suppression_set(list_id, exclude_silent_days)` — merges the global `Unsubscribe` table with an opt-in "silent users" bucket (emails sent ≥ `SEND_SILENT_THRESHOLD_CAMPAIGNS` distinct campaigns in the past N days with **no** `open`/`click` events).
- `verify_unsubscribe_sla(sla_hours)` — Yahoo 2-day SLA health check: scans recent `unsubscribe` / `spamreport` tracking events and reports any that haven't been honoured in the `Unsubscribe` table.

`ScheduleSendRequest.exclude_silent_days` (`edm-backend/app/api/campaigns_send.py`) threads through to `send_service.create_send_task`. Marketing/transactional domain split is enforced inside the preflight (overlap with the gate above).

## Config / env

`edm-backend/app/config.py` + `.env.example` got the Phase 4 knobs: `SEND_DAILY_QUOTA_LIMIT`, `SEND_MIN_VARIANTS`, `SEND_SILENT_THRESHOLD_CAMPAIGNS`, `SEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_SLA_HOURS`, `SEND_SPAM_RATE_WARN`, `SEND_SPAM_RATE_HARD_STOP`, `SEND_BOUNCE_RATE_DOWNSCALE`, `SEND_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SECONDS`. `SEND_WINDOW_HOURS` was already there; now it drives the dynamic stale threshold.

## Verified end-to-end

- Preflight rejects empty content / missing list / too few variants / marketing-on-transactional.
- `exclude_silent_days=30` correctly drops 5-of-20 recipients when 5 have been sent ≥ 6 distinct campaigns without engaging.
- Seeding 2 spamreport events against 4 delivered logs puts `spam_rate = 50%`, which the monitor auto-pauses; `resume_task` moves the task back to `queued`.
- Stale threshold = `SEND_WINDOW_HOURS * 1.5 * 60 = 360 min` at default 4h window.

### 🤖 Agent

The first run surfaces a real design-tension in the plan: with the plan's literal per-minute caps (variant×domain = 10/min, gmail = 50/min, etc.) a 500k/4h blast can't mathematically complete. Good, we caught a real issue: my TokenBucket capacity was allowed to grow monotonically with rate, letting peak 1-second throughput reach `rate + capacity = 180` when rate=90. Fix it to derive capacity from rate with a short burst window:

 I'm seeing the core issue now—when `set_rate()` is called, the capacity only increases via `max(self.capacity, new_rate)`, which means it never decreases. This causes unbounded growth when the rate scales up and down repeatedly, especially since burst accumulates on top of the ever-growing capacity. I think the issue is in how my simulation loop interacts with the refill logic. When `try_acquire` checks if we need to wait, it refills the bucket, and then later when `consume` is called after advancing the clock, it refills again based on that time advance. So if there's been a long idle period where tokens accumulated to capacity, we could consume a full burst of 90 tokens in rapid succession, but I'm still seeing a peak of 130 somewhere in the stats—maybe the measurement is capturing something about how tokens are being counted across multiple refill cycles or there's an off-by-one in how I'm tracking the peak rate. I see the real issue now: with a token bucket design, the peak rate over 1 second equals capacity plus the refill amount (rate), which is why I hit 180 tokens available. To keep the peak within my slack tolerance of 1.1x, I need to set capacity much smaller than the rate—something like `capacity = max(rate * 0.2, 1)` so the maximum burst per second stays around 1.2x the steady-state rate instead of doubling it.

But there's a catch with very low rates like the variant_domain at 6.67/s: if capacity becomes 0.33 tokens, I can never accumulate enough for a single message. The better approach is to use a tiered formula—allow `capacity = max(rate, 1)` for rates below 10/s to permit some batching, and `capacity = rate * 0.2` for higher rates. Though I also need to be careful when `set_rate` updates the capacity, since the current logic of `self.capacity = max(old_capacity, new_rate)` would jump capacity to 90 when the rate increases, defeating the whole fix.

The real solution is to recompute capacity proportionally whenever the rate changes, using a formula like `capacity = max(rate * 0.1, 1.0)` to give a 100ms burst window for fast rates while maintaining a 1-token floor for slow ones. I also need to clamp any existing tokens to the new capacity so stale tokens don't linger above the cap. Let me trace through the math: at 35/s, capacity becomes 3.5 (peak 1s ≈ 38.5 msg/s), and at 90/s, capacity becomes 9 (peak 1s ≈ 99 msg/s, slightly over the 1.1× slack but acceptable).  I'm seeing the problem now — when bounce rates stay above the threshold, the system keeps downscaling by 0.7 every 30 seconds, and after just 10 iterations it hits the floor of 1.0 requests per second, completely choking throughput. The real issue is that continuous downscaling without recovery creates a death spiral once bounces persist above the 2% threshold.

My test assertion about completing 50k messages in 4 hours fails in this scenario because a broken list will never recover — the monitor is doing its job by throttling, but my test shouldn't expect completion when the bounce rate is actively triggering downscales. I need to make the throughput assertion conditional: skip it whenever injected bounces exceed the threshold, since the feedback loop is intentionally preventing further damage.

动作 |\n|---|---|---|\n| `bounce_rate = bounced / sent` | > 2% (`SEND_BOUNCE_RATE_DOWNSCALE`) | `global_bucket.rate *= 0.7` |\n| SMTP 4xx 软失败率 | > 5% | `global_bucket.rate *= 0.7` |\n| `spam_rate = spamreport / delivered` | ≥ 0.1% (`SEND_SPAM_RATE_WARN`) | WARN 告警 + **不允许 upscale** |\n| `spam_rate` | ≥ 0.3% (`SEND_SPAM_RATE_HARD_STOP`) | **任务置 `paused`**，人工介入才能续跑 |\n| 进度落后窗口且 bounce/spam 健康 | — | `global_bucket.rate *= 1.1`，不超过 `SEND_GLOBAL_RATE_PER_SEC_MAX` |\n\nOn-call 每日需要巡检的外部面板：\n1. [Gmail Postmaster Tools](https://postmaster.google.com/) — domain & IP reputation、认证通过率、投诉率\n2. 腾讯云 SES 控制台 → 发送数据 → 投递率 / 退信率 / 打开率\n3. 平台内 `GET /reports/overview?campaign_id=...` — 本地镜像的 bounce/spam 指标\n\n**红线数值速查**：\n- Gmail：**投诉率 ≥ 0.3%** 会被直接降权；持续 ≥ 0.1% 要主动降量\n- Gmail 日发 > 5000 封到 gmail.com / googlemail.com 收件人就必须 SPF+DKIM+DMARC 三项全对齐\n- Yahoo bulk sender：日发 > 5000 强制 DMARC + One-click unsubscribe + 2 日内处理退订\n- 硬退信率（permanent bounce）持续 > 2% 是\"名单基本是坏的\"的信号，立即停发清单\n\n### 6. 压测与复盘\n\n- **本地仿真**：`edm-backend/stress_test_bulk_send.py`\n  - 默认 50 万虚拟收件人 + warmed profile + 虚拟时钟，秒级完成\n  - `--bounce-rate 0.03` 注入 3% 退信验证降速闭环\n  - `--spam-rate 0.005` 注入 0.5% 投诉验证 hard-stop\n  - `--profile plan-literal` 用 plan §2.1 冷启动档（gmail=50/min, variant×domain=10/min）验证 warmup\n  - `--asyncio-smoke` 用 `MockSESClient` 实跑一小批（默认 2000）验证协程形态\n- **上线前必跑**：\n  1. `warmed` profile 默认参数 → 仿真虚拟耗时 ≤ 4h × 1.15 buffer\n  2. `--bounce-rate 0.03` → 至少 1 次 downscale 且最终 rate < target\n  3. `--spam-rate 0.005` → hard_stop 触发，任务 paused\n  4. `--asyncio-smoke --asyncio-n 2000` → 真 MockSES 跑完，rate ≈ target\n- **生产复盘**：每次 50 万+ campaign 完成后，把实际 bounce/spam/打开率与 Postmaster 数据导到一张\n  复盘文档里，观察三级桶有无某一级成为瓶颈、ramp 是否过保守或过激进，再调 `.env`。\n\n---"

resp.active_ratio\n    : 0;\n\n  return {\n    total,\n    bySegment: resp.by_segment ?? {},\n    byGroup: resp.by_group ?? {},\n    byLang,\n    byPlan,\n    activeRatio,\n    topLanguages,\n    paidRatio,\n    audienceSummary: resp.audience_summary ?? '',\n    segmentProfiles,\n    groupProfiles,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction buildStatsFromQuery(resp: BackendQueryResponse): RecipientStats {\n  return {\n    total: resp.total,\n    valid: resp.total,\n    duplicates: 0,\n    unsubscribed: 0,\n    bySegment: resp.by_segment ?? {},\n    byLang: resp.by_lang ?? {},\n    byPlan: resp.by_plan ?? {},\n    sample: (resp.sample ?? []).map((s) => ({\n      email: s.email,\n      segment: s.segment ?? '',\n      lang: s.lang,\n      plan: s.plan,\n    })),\n  };\n}\n\nfunction buildStatsFromUpload(resp: BackendCsvUploadResponse): RecipientStats {\n  return {\n    total: resp.total,\n    valid: resp.valid,\n    duplicates: resp.duplicates,\n    unsubscribed: resp.unsubscribed,\n    formatErrors: resp.format_errors,\n    bySegment: resp.by_segment ?? {},\n    byLang: resp.by_lang,\n    byPlan: resp.by_plan,\n    sample: [],\n  };\n}\n\n// ── RTK Query endpoints (now all hitting real /api/recipients/*) ────────\n\nfunction extractErrorMessage(err: FetchBaseQueryError | undefined): string {\n  if (!err) return '网络错误';\n  const data = err.data as { detail?: string | Array<{ msg?: string }> } | undefined;\n  if (typeof data?.detail === 'string') return data.detail;\n  if (Array.isArray(data?.detail)) {\n    return data.detail.map((d) => d?.msg ?? 'invalid').join('; ');\n  }\n  return `请求失败 (${err.status})`;\n}\n\nexport const recipientApi = createApi({\n  reducerPath: 'recipientApi',\n  baseQuery: fetchBaseQuery({\n    baseUrl: '/api',\n    prepareHeaders: (headers) => {\n      const token = localStorage.getItem('edm_token');\n      if (token) headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`);\n      return headers;\n    },\n  }),\n  endpoints: (builder) => ({\n    queryRecipients: builder.mutation<QueryRecipientsResponse, RecipientQuery>({\n      queryFn: async (query, _api, _extra, fetchWithBQ) => {\n        const body = {\n          segments: query.segments ?? queryParams: Record<string, unknown> }\n    >({\n      queryFn: async ({ campaignId, queryParams }, _api, _extra, fetchWithBQ) => {\n        const resp = await fetchWithBQ({\n          url: '/recipients/query/confirm',\n          method: 'POST',\n          body: { campaign_id: campaignId, query_params: queryParams },\n        });\n        if (resp.error) {\n          return {\n            error: {\n              status: resp.error.status,\n              data: { message: extractErrorMessage(resp.error) },\n            } as FetchBaseQueryError,\n          };\n        }\n        const payload = resp.data as { list_id: string };\n        return { data: { listId: payload.list_id } };\n      },\n    }),\n\n    uploadCsvRecipients: builder.mutation<QueryRecipientsResponse, { file: File }>({\n      queryFn: async ({ file }, _api, _extra, fetchWithBQ) => {\n        const form = new FormData();\n        form.append('file', file);\n        const resp = await fetchWithBQ({\n          url: '/recipients/upload',\n          method: 'POST',\n          body: form,\n        });\n        if (resp.error) {\n          return {\n            error: {\n              status: resp.error.status,\n              data: { message: extractErrorMessage(resp.error) },\n            } as FetchBaseQueryError,\n          };\n        }\n        const payload = resp.data as BackendCsvUploadResponse;\n        return {\n          data: {\n            stats: buildStatsFromUpload(payload),\n            audienceProfile: buildAudienceProfile(payload),\n            listId: payload.list_id,\n          },\n        };\n      },\n    }),\n  }),\n});\n\nexport const {\n  useQueryRecipientsMutation,\n  useConfirmRecipientQueryMutation,\n  useUploadCsvRecipientsMutation,\n} = recipientApi;\n"

**但是这些破绽还没堵上（= 真正需要"降级方案"的地方）：**

1. **数据库查询路径没有 minimal 检测。** `[edm-backend/app/services/recipient_service.py](edm-backend/app/services/recipient_service.py)` 的 `create_list_from_query`（走 `/recipients/query/confirm` 入口）默认 `subscription_plan=u.get("plan", "Free")`，然后 `build_behavior_tags` 把缺失的 `active_days_ago` 当作 `0`——结果所有缺字段的用户会被 `detect_lifecycle_stage` 判成 `onboarding`，被错分到 `new_users` 组。这是你图里"新注册用户 59 人"这种虚假分组出现的根因之一。

2. **Strategy Planner 对 `lang_*` 组依然跑完整 LLM 调用。** `[edm-backend/app/services/ai_service.py](edm-backend/app/services/ai_service.py)` 的 `plan_strategies` 会产出 `tone / content_focus / urgency_level / frequency_hint / avoid_list / acceptance_criteria` 全套字段。前端会把这些渲染成图里那种"语气-温情关怀 / 低紧迫 / 频率-每周1次"的密密麻麻的标签墙——即使底下是盲发模式。

3. **Agent 0（Audience Selector）不知道自己处在 minimal 数据环境。** 它可能写 reasoning 说"面向活跃付费用户"——但数据根本没有付费维度，下游会被 CSV 路径强改回 `language_only`，Agent 0 的 reasoning 和最终分组对不上。

所以降级方案的核心是把这三个破绽堵上：**minimal 状态要从数据入口一路冒泡到 Agent 0/1 甚至 UI**。

## 我需要你拍板的两件事

方案实现形态主要取决于这两点，回答后我再出 plan：

 现在我理清了整个系统的全貌。让我梳理一下数据流和降级方案的具体实现路径：有两个数据入口，一个是通过 CSV 上传的 `POST /recipients/upload` 端点，它会调用 `recipient_service.parse_and_import_csv`，这里已经有了最小化数据检测机制来识别仅包含邮箱和语言的情况，并相应地标记数据完整度和分组策略。

另一个是 `POST /recipients/query/confirm` 端点，它从数据库或模拟数据源查询用户，返回的用户对象包含完整的订阅计划和活跃度信息，然后传入 `build_audience_profile` 进行处理。

在实际的生产数据库中，Recipient 表虽然定义了 `subscription_plan` 等字段，但这些字段实际上没有数据填充，真实数据库里只有 `email` 和 `lang` 两个字段有值。当 AudienceProfile 的分组数据被传给 Strategy Planner 时，它会接收到包含字符摘要、关键特征、平均标签、付费比例和热门计划等信息的分组概览。

对于语言分组，系统已经特殊处理，只输出人数、语言类型和数据缺失的说明，但 Strategy Planner 仍然会被调用来生成策略维度的输出。

现在我看到了两个关键的问题。首先，数据库查询路径缺少对最小数据完整性的检测——如果真实数据库返回的用户缺少计划、活跃天数或注册天数这些字段，系统会默认将它们当作 `Free/0/0` 处理，导致生命周期检测错误地将这些用户分类为新手探索期，进而产生完全不符合事实的策略建议。其次，即使分组数据全是语言分组，Strategy Planner 仍然会被调用来执行 LLM 推理。

虽然 Writer 的提示词已经阻止了虚假的个性化称呼，但 Agent 1 仍然会输出看起来很丰富的字段，前端会按这些字段渲染，误导操作人员以为系统基于真实用户画像做了分析。

还有一个问题是 Audience Selector 不知道数据层是最小化的，可能会选择基于支付活动的分组策略，但后端在处理 CSV 时会强制改回语言分组，导致前端展示的分组理由与实际分组不一致。最后，前端 UI 仍然会渲染所有的策略标签字段，即使底层实际上只有语言分组。

一个真正干净的降级方案应该在数据库查询入口就检测可用字段，自动切换到语言分组模式。

Agent 0 需要感知到数据限制，跳过无法生成的字段。Agent 1 在最小化数据下应该使用一个固定的广播策略框架，而不是调用 LLM，前端也要显示一个降级徽章来表明当前是盲发模式。

为了确定实施范围，我需要问用户几个关键问题，比如数据库的实际结构是什么，这会决定降级检测逻辑应该写在哪里。

其次是降级的程度——可以是只改 Strategy Planner 使用规则化 skeleton，或者更深层的改动包括 Audience Selector 和整个 pipeline 的降级模式。最后要确认真实数据库的查询方式，因为目前代码可能还在用 mock 数据，这会影响是否需要修改数据模型。

从用户的措辞来看，他对代码分层的理解可能还不够深入，所以应该优先选择改动最小、对现有架构影响最小的方案。

但我需要先问清楚两个关键问题：用户说的"数据库只有 email 和语言"具体指什么范围，以及前端 UI 上希望呈现什么样的降级效果。我先不做假设，直接向用户提出这些核心问题。

### 🤖 Agent

 所以用户选择了方案 B，这意味着需要在数据库查询路径加入 minimal 检测，Agent 0 在 minimal 模式下跳过或使用固定的 language_only 设置，Strategy Planner 采用 skeleton 方式，前端显示"盲发模式"徽章。但现在发现了个问题——表结构里根本没有 subscription_plan、registered_at 和 last_active_at 这些字段，所以需要先更新 schema 迁移。这里有个核心矛盾需要理清。

用户说 `schema_has_no_plan` 意味着 Recipient 表没有 subscription_plan 列，但代码里明确定义了这个字段。我觉得可能有几种情况：要么用户的描述不够精确，表里其实有这列但没人写入数据；要么线上生产数据库还是旧版 schema，代码层面有但迁移没上线；要么用户想把这列删掉走极简 schema。从用户说"现在版本的数据库只分邮箱和语言"这句话来看，我倾向于认为他觉得业务上不需要这个字段，可能没意识到 ORM 层其实有定义。

最合理的推测是 Recipient 表 schema 上有 subscription_plan 列，但实际写入的数据都是默认值，所以在不依赖这些字段的前提下跑通系统，而不是真的去删除列。

关键是 `active_days_ago` 和 `registered_days_ago` 这两个字段根本不在 Recipient 表里——它们是查询时临时计算出来的，不是表字段。所以"schema_has_no_plan"在用户理解里更可能是"我们数据库真的没有这些时间戳字段，只有 email 和语言是业务可信的"。

降级方案就很清楚了：把 Recipient 表视为只含 email、语言和发送追踪字段，所有 AI 路径都不要假设还有其他维度。不动 schema 避免迁移风险，改成所有从真实数据库查询出来的用户都进入最小化模式，但保留上传 enrichment 路径让 operator 可以自己传入完整数据，同时在 API 层忽略 subscription_plan 列。

我需要澄清用户选"schema_has_no_plan"的真实意思——是指按 Recipient 表只有 email 和语言来设计逻辑，还是需要真的删除 subscription_plan 列？但这个细节其实不是关键瓶颈。

无论用户怎么选，我都可以把 schema 修改设为可选步骤，核心方案就是代码层面强制走最小化配置，不依赖那些缺失的字段——这样两种选择都能兼容。现在我需要看一下前端怎么渲染策略卡片，确保方案能覆盖整个流程。

### 🤖 Agent

信息够了。核心发现是：生产数据路径其实依赖 `query_mock_users`（见 `[ai_service.py:1418](edm-backend/app/services/ai_service.py)`），mock 天生带全字段，所以图里能渲染出完整的 payment_activity_matrix 分组。一旦换到真 `Recipient` 表（只有 `email/lang/subscription_plan(空)`）就立刻错分——这就是你想做降级方案的直觉来源。方案 B 的落点非常清晰，我出 plan。

 I'm getting clarity on the full picture now. The `Recipient` table actually has the `subscription_plan` column already, but those timestamp fields like `registered_at` and `last_active_at` were only generated temporarily by the mock query function and never persisted to the database. On the frontend side, I need to check what `StepAudience.tsx` is doing and how it connects to the rest of the flow.

The real issue is that `_auto_generate_impl` is completely dependent on `query_mock_users()` as a fake data source—production isn't even connected to the real database yet. That's why the dashboard shows those specific user counts broken down into eight segments; the mock data has all the fields populated, so users get properly categorized. But this reveals a bigger architectural problem: the entire pipeline relies on mock data, and switching to the real database would break everything since the actual `Recipient` table only has reliable `email` and `lang` fields. The user's real intent is to migrate from mock to real data while accepting that the pipeline will degrade until those missing fields get backfilled—so I need to design a minimal degradation strategy that lets it run with just the core fields available.

The approach is to bubble up the "minimal state" explicitly from the data source layer all the way through to the agents and frontend, never guessing at missing dimensions. I'm creating a new production query path that returns only `email + lang` from the real database, explicitly marking everything else as `UNKNOWN_PLAN` or `None` rather than using default values. Then I'm adding a settings flag to switch between mock and database sources, and updating the dispatcher in `_auto_generate_impl` to route through the same source abstraction. In the `Audience` layer, I'll add detection logic to check if all users are in this minimal state and handle the degradation appropriately.

For the Agent layer, I'm introducing an `AudienceDataCapability` enum that tracks whether we're working with full or minimal data, passing this explicitly to the Agent 0 prompt so it understands the constraints. The system prompt gets a new parameter that, when in minimal mode, forces `grouping_strategy` to `language_only` and restricts query parameters to only `langs` and default exclusions. The backend adds a protective sanitization step that converts any non-`language_only` strategy to `language_only` in minimal mode and logs a warning about the override.

For the SSE event, I'm adding a `data_capability` field to `audience_selected` so the frontend can display a "blind send mode" badge to the user.

For Agent 1's strategy planner, I'm detecting when all group IDs follow the `lang_*` pattern and skipping the LLM call entirely, instead generating a skeleton strategy directly. This skeleton approach creates a single shared `GroupStrategy` across all language groups with fixed values like `detected_intent="feature_announcement"`, a professional-friendly tone, 2-3 key points extracted from the material, low urgency, and empty personalization hints. The avoid list explicitly prevents language around individual behavior or subscription status, and acceptance criteria are simplified to just three checks: material fidelity, no placeholder/urgency words in subject, and neutral salutations.

The strategy completion event gets a `degraded: true` flag to signal this mode to the frontend.

For the content writer, I'm keeping the existing neutral addressing logic unchanged since it already handles unknown audiences well.

On the frontend side, when `data_capability` is `"minimal_email_lang"`, I'm showing a prominent banner explaining blind send mode, and in the strategy card, if `degraded` is true, I'm collapsing the 8-10 field labels down to just intent, tone, and the three acceptance criteria, tucking the rest into an expandable panel to avoid visual clutter.

For the database schema, I'm leaving the `subscription_plan` column untouched to avoid migration risk, but in minimal mode I'm explicitly setting it to `UNKNOWN_PLAN` when creating lists from queries.

When we eventually add new fields like `registered_at` and `last_active_at`, we'll use an Alembic migration to upgrade from minimal back to full capability.

For testing, I'm adding a new test file that validates the degradation flow end-to-end: checking that lists with no plan or timestamp data get grouped by language only, that the strategy planner returns skeleton responses without calling the LLM, that the content writer prompt includes the restrictions for member tiers, and that the full SSE stream properly signals both `data_capability` and `degraded` flags.

In that minimal case we:\n\n      * pick ``grouping_strategy=\"language_only\"`` so the resulting\n        ``group_id`` values are ``lang_*`` (and flow into the Writer's\n        blind-send salutation branch);\n      * persist ``subscription_plan=UNKNOWN_PLAN`` instead of defaulting to\n        ``\"Free\"``, which would be an unsafe guess;\n      * leave ``registered_at`` / ``last_active_at`` as NULL rather than\n        backfilling from a zero-days-ago placeholder.\n    \"\"\"\n    from app.services.audience_service import build_behavior_tags, _auto_group_users\n\n    capability = detect_audience_capability(users)\n    is_minimal = capability == CAPABILITY_MINIMAL\n    grouping_strategy = grouping_strategy_for_capability(\n        capability,\n        requested=query_params.get(\"grouping_strategy\") if isinstance(query_params, dict) else None,\n    )\n\n    recipient_list = RecipientList(\n        campaign_id=campaign_id,\n        source=\"database\",\n        total_count=len(users),\n        valid_count=len(users),\n        query_params=query_params,\n        status=\"ready\",\n    )\n    db.add(recipient_list)\n    await db.flush()\n\n    tags_list = [build_behavior_tags(u) for u in users]\n    group_map = _auto_group_users(users, tags_list, grouping_strategy)\n    idx_to_group: dict[int, str] = {}\n    for gid, indices in group_map.items():\n        for idx in indices:\n            idx_to_group[idx] = gid\n\n    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)\n    for i in range(0, len(users), BATCH_INSERT_SIZE):\n        batch_slice = users[i:i + BATCH_INSERT_SIZE]\n        for j, u in enumerate(batch_slice):\n            real_idx = i + j\n            # AI 自动选人路径把 snapshot 写回一条新 list：尽量保留\n            # 绝对时间，缺则回退成相对 days_ago → 推回绝对时间，方便下次\n            # query_users_from_db 继续按 active_within_days 过滤。\n            registered_at = u.get(\"registered_at\")\n            if not isinstance(registered_at, datetime):\n                registered_at = days_ago_to_datetime(u.get(\"registered_days_ago\"), now)\n            last_active_at = u.get(\"last_active_at\")\n            if not isinstance(last_active_at, datetime):\n                last_active_at = days_ago_to_datetime(u.get(\"active_days_ago\"), now)\n\n            if is_minimal:\n                plan_to_persist = UNKNOWN_PLAN\n            else:\n                plan_to_persist = u.get(\"plan\") or UNKNOWN_PLAN\n\n            db.add(Recipient(\n                list_id=recipient_list.id,\n                email=u[\"email\"],\n                segment=u.get(\"segment\") or None,\n                group_id=idx_to_group.get(real_idx, \"\"),\n                lang=u.get(\"lang\", \"en\"),\n                subscription_plan=plan_to_persist,\n                registered_at=None if is_minimal else registered_at,\n                last_active_at=None if is_minimal else last_active_at,\n            ))\n        await db.flush()\n\n    return recipient_list"

### 🤖 Agent

Task 2 需要在 Agent 0 跑之前知道数据能力。我先加一个 `probe_recipient_capability` 轻量 DB 探查，然后按 schema → prompt → service → SSE 顺序展开。

 Moving on to Task 2 now. I need to add a `data_capability` field to the `AudienceSelection` schema, update the prompt builder to accept this parameter with stricter instructions when set to minimal, and modify the service layer so `select_audience` passes the capability to the prompt while `_auto_generate_impl` pre-checks the capability first before calling `select_audience`.

For the SSE event, I'll add `data_capability` to the `audience_selected` payload, and when capability is minimal, I'll force `grouping_strategy="language_only"`.

The core challenge is that we need to know the data capability before Agent 0 runs, but currently Agent 0 determines the query parameters first. To solve this, I'm creating a helper function that probes the Recipients table at the start of `_auto_generate_impl` — it counts total recipients and checks what percentage have valid subscription plans or recent activity timestamps, then returns either "full" or "minimal" based on a threshold like 5%.

Actually, I'm reconsidering this approach because it adds complexity and an extra database round trip. Instead, I'll use a simpler two-stage approach: pass a rough capability estimate to Agent 0's system prompt based on a quick probe, let Agent 0 run and query the actual users, then detect the precise capability from the real results. Both values get passed downstream, with the frontend using the precise one.

For the implementation, I'll start by writing the lightweight probe function that runs just two count queries, then update `select_audience` to accept the data_capability parameter. Agent 0's prompt will include hard constraints when capability is minimal—forcing `language_only` grouping and preventing any reasoning about paid or active users. The backend will enforce this as a safety measure too, overriding any strategy Agent 0 produces and logging the override. After querying actual users, I'll run the capability detection again as a double-check, and include the data_capability field in the SSE event.

Now I need to implement the probe function and check the structure of ai_service.py.

 "new_string": "async def count_total_recipients(db: AsyncSession) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Quick check used by the API layer to produce the \"先上传 CSV\" error\n    when the database is still empty.\"\"\"\n    result = await db.execute(select(func.count()).select_from(Recipient))\n    return int(result.scalar() or 0)\n\n\nasync def probe_recipient_capability(db: AsyncSession) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Estimate the Recipient table's data capability before Agent 0 runs.\n\n    We can't wait for ``query_users_from_db`` to return the actual users\n    before deciding the Audience Selector prompt — the LLM needs to know\n    *before* picking a grouping_strategy whether it has behavioural\n    signals to work with. Two lightweight COUNT queries answer this:\n\n      1. How many rows have a meaningful ``subscription_plan`` (non-null,\n         non-empty, not ``\"unknown\"``)?\n      2. How many rows have a ``last_active_at`` timestamp?\n\n    If **either** signal exists on any row, the batch is treated as\n    ``full`` — even mixed batches benefit from the enrichment path for\n    the users that do have signal, and the blind-send branches will still\n    kick in per-group if a particular ``lang_*`` slice happens to carry\n    zero enriched rows. If both are zero across the table, we commit to\n    the blind-send presentation end-to-end.\n\n    Empty table → ``minimal_email_lang`` (Agent 0 will still run so the\n    UI can show the selector reasoning, but there will be no users to\n    send to anyway).\n    \"\"\"\n    paid_count_stmt = select(func.count()).select_from(Recipient).where(\n        Recipient.subscription_plan.isnot(None),\n        Recipient.subscription_plan != \"\",\n        Recipient.subscription_plan != UNKNOWN_PLAN,\n    )\n    paid_count = int((await db.execute(paid_count_stmt)).scalar() or 0)\n    if paid_count > 0:\n        return CAPABILITY_FULL\n\n    active_count_stmt = select(func.count()).select_from(Recipient).where(\n        Recipient.last_active_at.isnot(None),\n    )\n    active_count = int((await db.execute(active_count_stmt)).scalar() or 0)\n    if active_count > 0:\n        return CAPABILITY_FULL\n\n    return CAPABILITY_MINIMAL"
